text:
Ebon: Quick heads-up — morning canary for the new flow-gating algo showed a 95th jump on route 'query-embedding'. Target was 150ms, observed ~218ms. Anyone else?
Sasha: Yep, saw that. Short profiler run shows a lot more kernel handoffs during 2nd half of the window. Handoff+memcpy spikes around microbatch boundary.
Marta: KV hitrate dipped too during the spike window: before=0.88 -> during=0.80. Might be related to sampler/route key churn.
Raj: Do we have the kernel selection logs for those requests? curious if it switched to the fallback fp32 path.
Sasha: paste of relevant lines from runtime logs:

```
[12:03:17] route=query-embedding seq=512 microbatch=7 kernel=attn_cuda_v2 -> fallback=attn_cuda_fp32 memcpy=1.7ms
[12:03:17] route=query-embedding kv_hit=false prefetch=false
[12:03:18] route=query-embedding microbatch_end total=9 tokens=184
```

Sasha: So two things: 1) kernel switch triggered at longer seqs; 2) KV miss + no prefetch caused extra latency.
Ebon: Interesting. The flow-gating logic refills credits per-route and allows larger microbatches for high-throughput routes. Maybe we over-allocated for this route and pushed sequences into the kernel path that prefers a different kernel.
Marta: Agree. I can add a quick KV prewarm on route entry to bump hitrate; also add a metric to split kv_hit by microbatch index.
Raj: Short mitigation options:
- reduce route window from 200 tokens -> 120 tokens
- reduce max microbatches from 12 -> 8
- flip dynamic_flow=false for that route (instant rollback)

Which do we want to try first?
Sasha: Plan: I'll run a micro-canary with kernel_prefetch=true + max_microbatches=8 for the route. That tests both kernel path stability and KV prefetch effect.
perf-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert: route=query-embedding 95th latency exceeded threshold (target=150ms observed=218ms) — triggering watchlist.
Ebon: Sasha, run canary and post canary run id here. Marta, please push KV prewarm change to canary config. Raj, prepare the rollback toggle and the static_budget=150 token override.
Sasha: Running profiler command now to reproduce locally:

```
./tools/profiler --route query-embedding --window 30s --top 50 --enable-kernel-logging
```

Sasha: I'll capture kernel selection histogram + microbatch sizes. Expect results in ~10m.
Marta: Added a KV prewarm toggle (kv_prewarm=true) to the canary config and deployed. Also added a prometheus metric kv_hit_by_mb_index.
Raj: Rollback toggle ready in /ops/flags: dynamic_flow.query-embedding=false, static_budget.query-embedding=150. Will hold off until Sasha posts canary id.
Ebon: If the kernel_prefetch canary doesn't reduce 95th within 15% of target, we should flip rollback. Also capture a trace with TRACE_ID and attach.
Sasha: Canary run id: canary-2026-03-18-01. Early numbers: 95th down to 168ms, kv_hit improved to 0.85. Kernel_fallback events reduced by ~60% in the sample.
Marta: Nice. I'll keep watching kv_hit_by_mb_index for regressions.
Raj: If that stabilizes we'll consider permanent changes: lower default window for this route and add kernel_prefetch as opt-in for long-seq routes.
Ebon: Thanks — looks like the tuning leans toward conservative per-route windows + KV prewarm + kernel_prefetch. Follow-ups: Sasha post full profile, Marta roll the kv metric to dashboards, Raj get rollback runbook added to the incident doc.
Sasha: Will post profile dump (gz) and a short summary in ~30m. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Note: alert cleared for the canary group after reduction below threshold for 10m.
Ebon: Perfect. Good triage — this was a subtle interaction between batching heuristic + kernel selection + KV behavior. We'll write a short postmortem if the permanent rollout proceeds.
